overview: 46 official Qs; 33 of them in 2025 Mains, the rest 2008, 2017, 2019, 2024. 2025 style: direct one-liners on purpose/primary goal of an Act, body or technique, NOT-questions, and matching (waste methods, pollutant–effect, pollution–source). Eco-friendly agriculture (11) and solid-waste disposal (8) carry the most.

possibility.what_they_ask: Method–function and method–pros/cons matching, waste type–disposal matching, goal of MSW Rules 2000, zero-waste city, Swachh Survekshan pairs, trans-boundary waste issue
Bhopal gas, natural vs man-made source, primary urban source
Meaning of high BOD, high coliform, BIS pH range for drinking water

Pollutant cutting blood oxygen (CO), pollution–pollutant matching (marble cancer, biomagnification), pollution–source matching
Year of EPA, purpose of Air Act/NGT, first CETP year, which is NOT an alternative method
AP law on borewells (APWALTA), which programme controls industrial emissions (NCAP)
Regulator of GMOs (GEAC), main environmental concern (gene flow), GM mustard developer, illegal Bt cultivation states

traps.trap: Monitoring body offered for an adjudicating body [regulator vs court]
traps.spot: Purpose questions on NGT, Air Act, GEAC with function options
traps.fix: NGT decides environmental cases; CPCB/SPCB monitor and set standards; GEAC approves GMO release; FSSAI = GM food
traps.pyq: 'Monitor industrial pollution levels' → handle environmental cases [mains-2025-paper2#77]; 'FSSAI' → GEAC [mains-2025-paper2#88]

traps.fix: High BOD = more organic/microbial pollution; coliforms = sewage (and go with higher BOD)
traps.pyq: 'Low level of Microbial Pollution' → high [mains-2017-paper1#39]; 'decreased BOD' → human waste [mains-2017-paper1#48]

traps.trap: Similar gas from the same family
traps.spot: CO vs CO2, MIC vs chlorine/ammonia
traps.fix: CO forms carboxyhaemoglobin; Bhopal 1984 = methyl isocyanate

traps.trap: Thermal or conventional method passed as biological/alternative
traps.fix: Bio- needs a living agent; burning and incineration are conventional thermal methods

traps.trap: Benefit dressed as a concern (or vice versa)
traps.fix: GM concern = gene flow to non-GM crops; reduced pesticide and higher yield are claimed benefits
traps.pyq: 'Reduced pesticide use' → cross-pollination with non-GM crops [mains-2025-paper2#87]

traps.trap: Acronym expanded with a look-alike word
traps.pyq: 'System of Renovation of Irrigation' → Rice Intensification [group2-2008-paper3#127]

traps.trap: Absolute claim in a benefit option
traps.fix: Organic yields are often lower; modern agriculture does deplete freshwater – judge the fact
traps.pyq: 'Higher crop yields in all conditions' → reduced chemicals, better soil [mains-2025-paper2#81]

traps.trap: Year of the trigger event offered for the Act
Scheme with a different pollution target
traps.spot: Flagship schemes listed for an air-quality aim
traps.fix: NCAP (2019) = air; PMUY = household LPG; SBM = sanitation; AMRUT = urban water/sewerage

techniques.name: Medium-of-entry matching [where does it go?]
techniques.how: For pollution–source or pollutant–effect matching, ask which medium or body system the pollutant enters, then pair.
techniques.example: Stack gas → air, sewage → water, fertiliser → soil, construction → noise → a-II, b-I, c-III, d-IV [mains-2025-paper2#78]

techniques.name: Prefix decoding
techniques.how: Break technique names: in-situ = on site, ex-situ = moved; bio-augmentation = add microbes; phyto = plants; myco = fungi; pyro-lysis = heat without oxygen.
techniques.example: In-situ → treats material at the site; transport/excavation belong to ex-situ [mains-2025-paper2#123]

techniques.name: Purpose = the body's verb
techniques.how: Each institution has one verb: tribunal adjudicates, board monitors, committee appraises, programme reduces. Match the verb in options.
techniques.example: Air Act 1981 → maintain air quality standards; renewables/fertilisers are other domains [mains-2025-paper2#84]

techniques.name: Anchor-pair matching
techniques.how: Fix the surest pair, strike codes without it, then fix one more.
techniques.example: Incineration = burning (a-II) and pyrolysis = carbon fuels (b-I) leave only a-II, b-I, c-III, d-IV [mains-2025-paper2#143]

techniques.name: Natural vs anthropogenic sort
techniques.how: Classify all options; the odd class is the answer.
techniques.example: Factories, power stations, vehicles are man-made → forest fires [mains-2025-paper2#127]

techniques.name: Law chronology chain
techniques.how: Wildlife 1972 → Water 1974 → Forest 1980 → Air 1981 → EPA 1986 → Biodiversity 2002 → NGT 2010; place the stem's Act.

confusions.remember: High BOD = polluted; high DO = healthy
CO blocks haemoglobin; CO2 warms climate
On site (bioventing, biosparging) vs excavated (landfarming, biopile, bioreactor)
Add microbes vs add nutrients for native microbes
Burning with oxygen vs heating without oxygen to make fuels
Tribunal for cases vs board for monitoring and standards
GEAC environmental release; RCGM research; FSSAI GM food
ZBNF uses on-farm inputs (jeevamrutha), no purchased inputs; organic may use bought organic inputs
Soil-less nutrient solution vs plants + fish together
City air quality plan vs LPG to cut indoor smoke
Hazardous waste movement vs persistent organic pollutants
Acid rain on monuments vs DDT build-up up the food chain

anchors: Air Act 1981; Water Act 1974; NGT Act 2010
APWALTA 2002: AP law regulating borewells and water bodies
MSW Rules 2000 → SWM Rules 2016 (segregation at source)
Indore: zero-waste model, cleanest city in Swachh Survekshan
GEAC regulates GMO release; GM mustard DMH-11 from Delhi University
Sikkim: first 100% organic state, FAO Future Policy Gold Award 2018
SRI = System of Rice Intensification; ZBNF = Subhash Palekar
checklist: Which institution's verb fits: adjudicate, monitor, appraise, regulate?
Bio- or alternative method? Remove thermal/conventional options
Benefit vs concern: which is asked?
In matching, pair by the medium the pollutant enters
Year of event vs year of law
